story.value: Rhodium's name comes from the Greek word rhodon, meaning rose, because dilute solutions of its salts are rose colored.
Rhodium was discovered in 1803 by William Hyde Wollaston, an English chemist.
Wollaston obtained rhodium from a sample of platinum ore that came from South America.

uses.value: Rhodium is used to make electrical contacts.
Rhodium is used in catalytic converters.
Rhodium is mixed into platinum and palladium as an alloying agent to make them harder.
